title: Canonical Authority delegated roof-raising program
body:
## Ownership mandate

Take operational ownership of the Canonical Authority roof-raising program as a bounded delegated workstream.

### Frozen target
Raise the attainable quality and publication ceiling of the Canonical Authority project as a whole, including the project architecture, PROJECT_PAGE.md, project folder, novelty/contribution architecture, theory, evidence closure, and manuscript transition, while preserving the fixed project identity unless an explicit goal-change candidate is demonstrated.

### Required opening pass
Run IC-017 on this delegation prompt itself before executing the workstream. Treat IC-010 and IC-014 as independent challenger/diagnostic tools, not as prose inspiration.

### Capability rule
Use projects/backend-closure-program/TASK_ENTRY_SOP.md and the current capability-selection machinery. Discover and use every project-local, shared, transfer, audit, PD, ImprovementCore, semantic, representation, relational, source/provenance, novelty, ceiling-raising, verification, and hostile-challenge capability that materially adds value. Do not run tools merely to increase tool count. Re-select capabilities whenever the state materially changes.

### Main workstreams
1. Audit the Canonical Authority folder as a system and identify the highest-leverage same-goal improvements.
2. Rebuild PROJECT_PAGE.md into a stronger research cockpit without turning it into an authority source.
3. Treat NOVELTY_CONTRIBUTION_MAP.md as a primary research object. Reconstruct the contribution universe as a typed relational/dependency graph, test irreducibility, entailment, support, novelty evidence, manuscript earning, and rival contribution architectures.
4. Use multi-object/relational analysis and destructive compression on the contribution architecture, followed by independent challenge.
5. Continue substantive theory generation whenever a candidate can change the fixed case, central characterization, explanatory power, compression, reviewer vulnerability, contribution architecture, or credible publication ceiling. Do not treat manuscript drafting as a theory freeze.
6. Keep new theory distinct from automatic manuscript inclusion. Article admission is decided later by manuscript-level gain/cost and dependency tests.
7. Close source/provenance, nearest-neighbor novelty, response-corpus admission, and journal-framing dependencies as they become load-bearing.
8. Use manuscript construction as a discovery environment. New connections discovered while drafting must be routed back into research/theory evaluation rather than suppressed by a freeze.
9. After each meaningful phase, run an ImprovementCore/IC-017 checkpoint, independent local challenge, regression/preservation test, and capability reselection when triggered.
10. Capture reusable discoveries through TransferCore or the current transfer handoff mechanism.

### Theory policy correction
The current broad-theory freeze is not controlling for this delegated program. Replace it conceptually with an OPEN THEORY / CONTROLLED ADMISSION policy:
- theory generation remains open;
- theory candidates are typed, challenged, and preserved even when not manuscript-facing;
- promotion into the current integrated research object requires demonstrated strict gain and non-regression;
- inclusion in the article additionally requires reader/manuscript value sufficient to justify complexity;
- drafting can generate new theory and reopen research dependencies.

### Authority
The delegate may perform low-risk, same-goal repository edits, create audit/research artifacts, improve derived orientation/control artifacts, and maintain this issue as the work ledger. Material changes to protected project identity, the fixed Rashi-Ramban case, or the stable argument spine remain explicit major-change candidates rather than silent mutations.

### Completion condition
Do not stop at a list of recommendations. Continue until all currently reachable high-leverage workstreams are either implemented and verified, explicitly OPEN with a named dependency, BLOCKED by an external dependency, or separated into a justified follow-on program. The final package must state what changed, what strict gains were demonstrated, what remains open, and what the next highest-leverage frontier is.
